missed.text: For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered.

For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.

The Class IA and IB retro-reflectors of Red colour shall have minimum RI values in mcd∙lx-1 of 3.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 1.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°), 5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.8∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), and 2.5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°).
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux shall be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

When testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.

The retro-reflective devices shall have the resistance of the front surface to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.
The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1.

The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters of Table A6-1: cycle 1 with a black-standard thermometer (65 ± 3 °C) or cycle 4 with a black-panel thermometer (63 ± 3 °C), exposure periods of 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, irradiance 60 ± 2 W/m² broadband (300 to 400 nm) or 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m² narrowband (340 nm), relative humidity 50 ± 10 %.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall prevent the lamps from being inadvertently maladjusted under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected.
While all other functions with which a lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF, the lamp shall fulfill the photometric and colorimetric requirements.

While specific instructions are absent, the lamp shall not intentionally vary its photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

When there is doubt, the requirement that no red light shall be emitted to the front and no white light shall be emitted to the rear shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicator lamps and rear retro-reflectors (triangular or not) may be installed on movable components only if the conditions of paragraph 5.18.1. or 5.18.2. are met.

The lamps (devices) shall be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation when installed on a vehicle, where applicable.

The reversing lamp shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground, except that for category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm.
All categories of vehicles shall be equipped with two S1 or S2 category devices and one S3 or S4 category device.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 categories devices, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
Where the optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

The vertical angle of geometric visibility for S1 or S2 categories devices shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, except that (a) where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°; (b) where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1. and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° outwards to 45° inwards; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
When determining the unobstructed view of the apparent surface of the rear position lamp, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.

The electrical connections for rear position lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11, except that if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the electrical connection of the rear position lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle or the reciprocally incorporated part of it may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.
While daytime running lamps are not switched ON, the rear position lamp shall have a mandatory closed-circuit tell-tale.
The closed-circuit tell-tale of the rear position lamps shall be combined with that of the front position lamps; this requirement does not apply while the daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamp shall be mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector shall be permitted to have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.

The electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) conforming to a type approved under this Regulation shall have an approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. affixed to it, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.
The ESA representative of its type shall have measured values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, below the type approval limits.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
The ESA representative of its type shall have a measured value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, below the type approval limits.
The emission of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation by the method(s) as described in Annex 9.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band are given in Table 2a.

The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band is as given in Table 2b.

The immunity of ESA representative of this type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The starting profile shall be tested according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For the 24 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.

For pulse 3b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +75 V (12V system) or +150 V (24V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

The test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
The light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

The specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

Where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used and several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.

The light source module and the lamp shall both have marks from the same applicant, where the approval mark on the light source module does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii) in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The component shall have the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) affixed on it.

The position lamps or daytime running lamps, which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, shall be permitted.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) shall not be required to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, when the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

If any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source fails, then the single lamp shall ensure that at least one of the following provisions applies: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.
The lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) shall have all measurements made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
Unless otherwise specified, the lamp shall be operated for testing at a supply voltage at the lamp of 6.75 V (6 Volt systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt systems) or 28 V (24 Volt systems).
The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.
When reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps are operated for 1 minute and for 10 minutes, the luminous intensities shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

The luminous intensities for all other lamps (other than those mentioned in 1.2.1), measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation, or after photometric stability has occurred, shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

The luminous intensity distribution shall, depending on the light source technology and in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1, where the luminous intensity distributions at a point in time may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate of the lamp (function) under consideration.

extra.text: An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every rear combination lamp ESA conforming to a type approved under UN Regulation No. 10; no such marking is required if the lamp's electrical/electronic system is built into a vehicle approved as a unit.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of production samples of the ESA-approved lamp: verify an approval mark per paragraph 5.3. is affixed. Pass if the mark is present on every unit; not applicable if the lamp is approved only as part of a vehicle type.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall be tested for conducted emissions.
extra.test_case: UN R10 Annex 10 method for transient conducted emissions on the supply lines, with lamp functions switched on and off. Pass if the transient amplitudes stay within the limits of R10 paragraph 6.8.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
extra.test_case: UN R10 Annex 9 ESA radiated immunity methods at the field strengths of R10 paragraph 6.7, with functions monitored per the test plan. Pass if there is no degradation of the stop, rear position or reversing lamp functions, e.g. no unintended switching, flicker or loss of light output beyond the defined criteria.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.
extra.test_case: UN R10 Annex 10 conducted transient immunity test pulses on the supply lines, at the test levels of R10 paragraph 6.9. Pass if the functional status criteria are met and the lamp functions are not impaired.

extra.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 broadband radiated emission test, 75-400 MHz; pass if all measured values are below the log-increasing limit line from 52 dBµV/m at 75 MHz to 63 dBµV/m at 400 MHz (Appendix 6).

extra.text: On the rear combination lamp ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
extra.test_case: Compare Annex 7 broadband results across 30-1,000 MHz for each operating lamp function with the paragraph 6.5.2.1 limits; pass if every measured value is below the limit (no margin exceedance).

extra.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 narrowband measurement, 75-400 MHz; pass if measured level is below the limit line increasing logarithmically from 42 dB µV/m at 75 MHz to 53 dB µV/m at 400 MHz (Appendix 7).

extra.text: For vehicles with 12 V systems, the positive transient pulse amplitude conducted by the rear combination lamp onto the supply lines shall not exceed +75 V.
extra.test_case: Perform the ISO 7637-2 test per Annex 10 with a 12 V supply. Pass if the measured maximum positive pulse amplitude is ≤ +75 V.

extra.text: For vehicles with 12 V systems, the negative transient pulse amplitude conducted by the rear combination lamp onto the supply lines shall not exceed -100 V.
extra.test_case: Perform the ISO 7637-2 test per Annex 10 with a 12 V supply. Pass if the measured maximum negative pulse amplitude does not exceed -100 V in magnitude.

extra.text: When tested by the stripline method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 stripline, 20 to 400 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation of the immunity related functions at 60 V/m over at least 90 % of the test frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the stripline method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 stripline, 20 to 400 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation of the immunity related functions at 50 V/m at all frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the TEM cell method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 75 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 TEM cell, 20 to 200 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation at 75 V/m over at least 90 % of the test frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the TEM cell method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 TEM cell, 20 to 200 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation at 62,5 V/m at all frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the bulk current injection (BCI) method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 BCI on the harness, 20 to 400 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation at 60 mA over at least 90 % of the test frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the bulk current injection (BCI) method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 BCI, 20 to 400 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation at 50 mA at all frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the ALSE method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 30 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 ALSE, 80 to 2,000 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation at 30 V/m over at least 90 % of the test frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the ALSE method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 10 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 ALSE, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation at 10 V/m over at least 90 % of the test frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the ALSE method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 ALSE, 80 to 2,000 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation at 25 V/m at all frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the ALSE method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 ALSE, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation at 8 V/m at all frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the reverberation chamber method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 21 V/m in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber, LUF to 2,000 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation at 21 V/m over at least 90 % of the test frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the reverberation chamber method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 7 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation at 7 V/m over at least 90 % of the test frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the reverberation chamber method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber, LUF to 2,000 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation at 18 V/m at all frequencies.

extra.text: When tested by the reverberation chamber method of Annex 9, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz. Pass if there is no degradation at 6 V/m at all frequencies.

extra.text: When measured according to paragraph 6.5.2.1. (method of Annex 7) with a 120 kHz bandwidth, the broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m, where F is the frequency in MHz.
extra.test_case: Broadband radiated emission test per Annex 7 (ALSE, antenna at 1 m), lamp operated in its emitting modes, 120 kHz measurement bandwidth, scan 30-75 MHz; pass if all measured values are at or below 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m (62 dBµV/m at 30 MHz falling to 52 dBµV/m at 75 MHz).

extra.text: When measured according to paragraph 6.5.2.1. (method of Annex 7) with a 120 kHz bandwidth, the broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the limit E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m, where F is the frequency in MHz.
extra.test_case: Broadband radiated emission test per Annex 7 (ALSE, antenna at 1 m), lamp operated in its emitting modes, 120 kHz measurement bandwidth, scan 75-400 MHz; pass if all measured values are at or below 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m (52 dBµV/m at 75 MHz rising to 63 dBµV/m at 400 MHz).

extra.text: When measured according to paragraph 6.5.2.1. (method of Annex 7) with a 120 kHz bandwidth, the broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the constant limit E = 63 dBµV/m.
extra.test_case: Broadband radiated emission test per Annex 7 (ALSE, antenna at 1 m), lamp operated in its emitting modes, 120 kHz measurement bandwidth, scan 400-1,000 MHz; pass if all measured values are at or below 63 dBµV/m.

extra.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8 (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.), the narrowband radiated emission limit of the ESA in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m, F in MHz, for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 ESA narrowband radiated emission test with 120 kHz bandwidth, ESA operated in all lamp functions; pass if the measured narrowband level at every frequency from 30 to 75 MHz is at or below 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m.

extra.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8 (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.), the narrowband radiated emission limit of the ESA in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m, F in MHz, for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 ESA narrowband radiated emission test with 120 kHz bandwidth, ESA operated in all lamp functions; pass if the measured narrowband level at every frequency from 75 to 400 MHz is at or below 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m.

extra.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8 (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.), the narrowband radiated emission limit of the ESA in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at E = 53 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 ESA narrowband radiated emission test with 120 kHz bandwidth, ESA operated in all lamp functions; pass if the measured narrowband level at every frequency from 400 to 1,000 MHz is at or below 53 dBµV/m.

extra.text: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 para 2.1: operate all lamp functions simultaneously at nominal supply voltage (maximum load); verify the operating state is recorded in the test report.

extra.text: The broadband radiated emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
extra.test_case: Sweep 30 to 1,000 MHz; pass if all readings are below the para 6.5 limits across the whole range.

extra.text: If peak detectors are used for the broadband emission measurement, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied to the quasi-peak limits given in paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10.
extra.test_case: Check the evaluation uses limits adjusted by 20 dB when a peak detector is used; pass if peak readings are within the corrected limit.

extra.text: During the narrowband emission test, the rear combination lamp (ESA) under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 para. 2; operate the lamp with the functions energised at nominal supply, preferably all functions on (maximum load); check that the test report records the operating mode.

extra.text: The narrowband emission limits shall apply to the rear combination lamp throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
extra.test_case: Scan 30 to 1,000 MHz in ALSE or OATS; pass if emissions are below paragraph 6.6.2.1 limits across the whole range.

extra.text: The narrowband emission measurements of the rear combination lamp shall be performed with an average detector.
extra.test_case: Verify measuring instrument detector setting is average for all readings.

extra.text: The frequency range and general test conditions for the rear combination lamp ESA immunity test shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Check that the test report references ISO 11452-1 for the frequency range and general conditions.

extra.text: The test conditions for the rear combination lamp ESA immunity test shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Audit the test setup (temperature, supply voltage, ground plane and similar conditions) against ISO 11452-1.

extra.text: In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation) with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth.
extra.test_case: Verify the generator settings: AM, 1 kHz, 80 per cent depth over 20 to 400 MHz.

extra.text: In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2) with Ton 3 µs and period 3,333 µs.
extra.test_case: Verify the generator settings: PM, Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs over 2,700 to 3,100 MHz.

extra.text: In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3) with Ton 500 µs and period 1,000 µs.
extra.test_case: Verify the generator settings: PM, Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs over 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz.

extra.text: As an alternative, the ESA may be tested installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4 using the BCI substitution method with the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA.
extra.test_case: If tested in-vehicle, verify ISO 11451-4 substitution method with the probe at 150 mm from the lamp.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
extra.test_case: Annex 10 method: apply ISO 7637-2 test pulses and ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the supply lines; the functional status of the lamp functions shall meet the ESA immunity criteria.

extra.text: Conducted transients emitted by the rear combination lamp ESA to the vehicle power supply shall be limited.
extra.test_case: Annex 10 paragraph 3 method: measure per ISO 7637-2 on the supply lines; emissions shall stay within the applicable limits.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection against approval documents: E-circle with correct country number present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4. (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp).
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: function symbols per paragraph 3.2.4. for each approved function are present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: "148R" followed by the correct two-digit series of amendments is present.

extra.text: If the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4.
extra.test_case: If applicable per approval: visual inspection that "D" is to the right of the relevant function symbol.

extra.text: If the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamps system, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4.
extra.test_case: If applicable per approval: visual inspection that "Y" is to the right of the relevant function symbol.

extra.text: On lamps with reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), the marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
extra.test_case: If reduced light distribution per Annex 3 paragraph 1.1. is claimed: visual inspection that the downward vertical arrow from a horizontal segment is present.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is used for the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after their installation.
extra.test_case: Inspection on vehicle: single approval mark visible after installation.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is used for the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
extra.test_case: Design review and disassembly check: no light-transmitting part can be removed without removing the approval mark.

extra.text: Each lamp of the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp) submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN Regulation No. 148.
extra.test_case: Compliance review against all requirements of paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN R148 (general and photometric/colorimetric requirements). Pass if every applicable requirement of paragraphs 4. and 5. is fulfilled for each lamp function.

extra.text: The rear position lamp function shall comply with the requirements of sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and the Annexes referenced in those sections) of UN Regulation No. 48, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, that are pertinent to rear position lamps on M1 vehicles, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Review of lamp design and documentation against UN R48 sections 5 and 6 (e.g. geometric visibility angles, orientation) for M1, evaluated during lamp type approval; pass if all requirements verifiable at lamp level are met.

extra.text: The lamps (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions of the rear combination lamp) shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured.
extra.test_case: Design review plus vibration/durability validation representative of vehicle use (e.g. OEM vibration profile); after exposure, all lamp functions shall operate correctly with no loosening, cracking, connector or LED failure.

extra.text: The stop lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the stop lamp apparent surface and optics; pass if no logo is present.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the reversing lamp apparent surface and optics; pass if no logo is present.

extra.text: In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
extra.test_case: Review LED circuit schematic and PCB layout to identify LED groups wired in series or with common failure; disconnect or open-circuit one LED per group and verify all LEDs of the group stop emitting. Pass: every group treated as one light source in the failure analysis of 4.6.1.2.

extra.text: In case of failure of any one light source in a rear position lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution in Annex 3, with the maximum intensities not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure as indicated in paragraph 6.10.8. of UN Regulation No. 48 shall be produced.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 3 with each single light source (group) failed in turn: all Annex 3 minimum values met; with all light sources lit: no maximum exceeded. Alternatively, simulate each single failure and verify the failure signal for the tell-tale is produced at the connector. Pass: one of the two options fulfilled for every single failure.

extra.text: If the failure provision is met by producing a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, the lamp shall only be used on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.
extra.test_case: Check that, where option (b) is used, the communication form note is present and the vehicle electrical architecture includes the failure tell-tale; verify tell-tale activation on vehicle by simulating a single light source failure. Pass: tell-tale activates.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, in case of failure of the variable intensity control the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category R2 shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control (open/short of control input, controller fault) and measure photometry per Annex 3. Pass: steady luminous intensity requirements of category R2 met automatically without intervention.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, in case of failure of the variable intensity control the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category S2 shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and measure photometry per Annex 3. Pass: steady luminous intensity requirements of category S2 met automatically.

extra.text: If the lamp uses replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall, regardless of the use of tool(s), not be interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.
extra.test_case: Attempt to swap modules of different functions or characteristics between their seats in the same housing, with and without tools. Pass if no swap is possible.

extra.text: Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems).
extra.test_case: Measure voltage at lamp connector during photometry; pass if 13.5 V for 12 V systems (6.75 V / 28 V for 6 V / 24 V systems).

extra.text: In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Operate lamp with applicant-specified control gear and settings during photometry; pass if test conditions match applicant specification.

extra.text: In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control and equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Operate lamp at applicant-specified supply conditions during photometry; pass if conditions match specification.

extra.text: The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the rear position lamp function in paragraph 5.
extra.test_case: Photometry at HV on both samples; pass if ≥ paragraph 5 minimum.

extra.text: The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the rear position lamp function in paragraph 5.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric scan over visible directions; pass if no value exceeds paragraph 5 maximum.

extra.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, the intensity of the rear position lamp shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the rear position lamp function in paragraph 5.
extra.test_case: Measure across Annex 2 geometric visibility angles; pass if ≥ paragraph 5 minimum.

extra.text: The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the reversing lamp function in paragraph 5.
extra.test_case: Photometry at HV on both samples; pass if ≥ paragraph 5 minimum.

extra.text: The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the reversing lamp function in paragraph 5.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric scan over visible directions; pass if no value exceeds paragraph 5 maximum.

extra.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, the intensity of the reversing lamp shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the reversing lamp function in paragraph 5.
extra.test_case: Measure across Annex 2 geometric visibility angles (incl. 45° outboard); pass if ≥ paragraph 5 minimum.

extra.text: If the applicant requests the additional test to verify visibility of red light towards the front, the maximum intensity of the red lamp functions in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction shall be not more than 2.5∙10-1 cd.
extra.test_case: Measure intensity over 165°–180° outboard H, -2.5° to +5° V, optionally with vehicle body influence; pass if max ≤ 0.25 cd.

extra.text: Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously and the intensity of the rear position lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.
extra.test_case: Measure intensities in ±5° V × ±10° H field with stop+position lit and with position lit alone; pass if ratio ≥ 5:1 at each point.

extra.text: If one or both of the reciprocally incorporated rear position and stop lamps contain more than one light source and are considered as a single lamp, the values to be considered for the 5:1 ratio shall be those obtained with all sources in operation.
extra.test_case: Perform ratio measurement with all LED sources of each function energised; pass if ratio ≥ 5:1.

extra.text: For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric check per relevant subparagraphs of 4.8 with the lamp's own LED modules installed and energised; colour within prescribed limits.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R1 (steady), its minimum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)) shall be 4∙10^0 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per Par. 4.8.3.1 (a); pass if intensity ≥ 4 cd.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R1 (steady) and used as a single lamp, its maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall not exceed 1.7∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per Par. 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if intensity ≤ 17 cd in all directions.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R1 (steady) and marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.), its maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall not exceed 8.5∙10^0 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per Par. 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if intensity ≤ 8.5 cd in all directions.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R1 (steady), its standard light distribution (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)) shall comply with Figure A3-I and Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Measure at grid points of Figure A3-I per Par. 4.8.3.1 (c); pass if values per Table A2-1 are met.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R1 (steady), its minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)) shall be 5∙10^-2 cd.
extra.test_case: Measure across the geometric visibility field per Par. 4.8.3.1 (d); pass if intensity ≥ 0.05 cd everywhere.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R2 (variable), its minimum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)) shall be 4∙10^0 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per Par. 4.8.3.1 (a); pass if intensity ≥ 4 cd.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R2 (variable) and used as a single lamp, its maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall not exceed 4.2∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per Par. 4.8.3.1 (b) under all variable intensity conditions; pass if intensity ≤ 42 cd.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R2 (variable) and marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.), its maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall not exceed 2.1∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per Par. 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if intensity ≤ 21 cd.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R2 (variable), its standard light distribution (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)) shall comply with Figure A3-I and Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Measure at grid points of Figure A3-I per Par. 4.8.3.1 (c); pass if values per Table A2-1 are met.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R2 (variable), its minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)) shall be 5∙10^-2 cd.
extra.test_case: Measure across the geometric visibility field per Par. 4.8.3.1 (d); pass if intensity ≥ 0.05 cd everywhere.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, a luminous intensity of up to 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement below -5° vertical; pass if intensity ≤ 60 cd there, and Table 4 maxima met elsewhere.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady), its minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd (60 cd).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per para. 4.8.3.1 (a) on both samples; pass if intensity is ≥ 60 cd where required.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady) and used as a single lamp, its maximum luminous intensity shall not exceed 2.60∙10^2 cd (260 cd).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per para. 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if no measured intensity exceeds 260 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady) and marked "D" (para. 3.3.2.5.2.), its maximum luminous intensity shall not exceed 1.30∙10^2 cd (130 cd).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per para. 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if no measured intensity exceeds 130 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1, its standard light distribution shall conform to Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Measurement at grid points of Figure A3-I per para. 4.8.3.1 (c); pass if each point meets the required percentage of minimum intensity.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1, the luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 shall be at least 3∙10^-1 cd (0.3 cd).
extra.test_case: Measurement across geometric visibility angles of Table A2-1 per para. 4.8.3.1 (d); pass if ≥ 0.3 cd throughout.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2 (variable), its minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd (60 cd).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per para. 4.8.3.1 (a) on both samples; pass if intensity is ≥ 60 cd where required.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2 (variable) and used as a single lamp, its maximum luminous intensity shall not exceed 7.30∙10^2 cd (730 cd).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per para. 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if no measured intensity exceeds 730 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2 (variable) and marked "D" (para. 3.3.2.5.2.), its maximum luminous intensity shall not exceed 3.65∙10^2 cd (365 cd).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per para. 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if no measured intensity exceeds 365 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2, the luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 shall be at least 3∙10^-1 cd (0.3 cd) in day condition.
extra.test_case: Measurement across geometric visibility angles of Table A2-1 in day mode per para. 4.8.3.1 (d); pass if ≥ 0.3 cd throughout.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2, the luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 shall be at least 7∙10^-2 cd (0.07 cd) in night condition.
extra.test_case: Measurement across geometric visibility angles of Table A2-1 in night mode per para. 4.8.3.1 (d); pass if ≥ 0.07 cd throughout.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp (category AR) supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 10.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1; pass if all Table 10 values (minimum, maximum, standard light distribution Figure A3-V) are met by each sample.

extra.text: The reversing lamp of category AR shall emit a minimum luminous intensity of 8.0∙10^1 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (a)).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at the reference axis/test points of the standard light distribution; pass if intensity ≥ 80 cd.

extra.text: The luminous intensity of the reversing lamp of category AR shall not exceed 3.00∙10^2 cd in or above the H-plane (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b)).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer scan in and above the H-plane; pass if maximum intensity ≤ 300 cd.

extra.text: The luminous intensity of the reversing lamp of category AR shall not exceed 6.00∙10^2 cd below the H-plane, down to 5°D (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b)).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer scan from H-plane down to 5°D; pass if maximum intensity ≤ 600 cd.

extra.text: The luminous intensity of the reversing lamp of category AR shall not exceed 8.00∙10^3 cd below 5°D (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b)).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer scan below 5°D; pass if maximum intensity ≤ 8000 cd.

extra.text: The light distribution of the reversing lamp of category AR shall comply with the standard light distribution defined in Figure A3-V (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (c)).
extra.test_case: Measure intensities at all Figure A3-V grid points; pass if each value meets the percentage of the minimum specified in Figure A3-V.

extra.text: If type approval is granted under the pair-only condition, the reversing lamp shall only be installed on the vehicle in a pair.
extra.test_case: Vehicle installation inspection; pass if two reversing lamps are fitted as a pair, consistent with item 9.1.3 of the communication form.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
extra.test_case: Failure tests per paragraph 4.6 (e.g. LED/light source failure simulation); pass if paragraph 4.6 criteria are met.

extra.text: The angles of geometric visibility of Annex 2 apply as shown to lamps mounted on the right side of the vehicle; for the lamp mounted on the left side of the vehicle the same angles shall be applied mirrored (inboard/outboard interchanged).
extra.test_case: Drawing/CAD review of the left and right lamps: confirm the inboard/outboard visibility angles are mirrored correctly for each side. Pass if each side meets the Table A2-1 values in its own inboard/outboard sense.

extra.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 80° outboard.
extra.test_case: Check geometric visibility of the apparent surface on a goniometer or CAD sight-line analysis, lamp installed per vehicle drawing. Pass if the apparent surface is unobstructed from 45° inboard to 80° outboard.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp (R1, R2) is mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the reduced minimum horizontal angles of 20° inboard / 80° outboard may be used only below the H-plane.
extra.test_case: Measure the H-plane mounting height. If below 750 mm, verify by goniometer or CAD that visibility is at least 45°/80° above the H-plane and at least 20°/80° below it.

extra.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.
extra.test_case: Goniometer or CAD sight-line check of the apparent surface, lamp installed. Pass if the surface is unobstructed from 15° up to 15° down.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp (R1, R2) is installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility shall be 15° above and 5° below.
extra.test_case: Measure the mounting height. If below 750 mm, verify visibility from 15° up to 5° down. Pass if unobstructed.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category MR and singular, it shall have minimum horizontal angles of 80° inboard / 80° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15° above / 5° below for an H-plane mounting height of less than 750 mm).
extra.test_case: Goniometer or CAD visibility check against these angles. Pass if all are met.

extra.text: If the rear position lamps are of category MR and installed as a pair, each lamp shall have minimum horizontal angles of 20° inboard / 80° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15° above / 5° below for an H-plane mounting height of less than 750 mm).
extra.test_case: Goniometer or CAD visibility check against these angles. Pass if all are met.

extra.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 45° outboard.
extra.test_case: Goniometer or CAD sight-line check of the apparent surface, lamp installed. Pass if unobstructed from 45° inboard to 45° outboard.

extra.text: If the stop lamp (S1, S2) is mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the reduced minimum horizontal angles of 20° inboard / 45° outboard may be used only below the H-plane.
extra.test_case: Measure the mounting height. If below 750 mm, verify at least 45°/45° above the H-plane and at least 20°/45° below it.

extra.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.
extra.test_case: Goniometer or CAD sight-line check. Pass if the apparent surface is unobstructed from 15° up to 15° down.

extra.text: If the stop lamp (S1, S2) is installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility shall be 15° above and 5° below.
extra.test_case: Measure the mounting height. If below 750 mm, verify visibility from 15° up to 5° down. Pass if unobstructed.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category MS and singular, it shall have minimum horizontal angles of 45° inboard / 45° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15° above / 5° below for an H-plane mounting height of less than 750 mm).
extra.test_case: Goniometer or CAD visibility check against these angles. Pass if all are met.

extra.text: If the stop lamps are of category MS and installed as a pair, each lamp shall have minimum horizontal angles of 0° inboard / 45° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15° above / 5° below for an H-plane mounting height of less than 750 mm).
extra.test_case: Goniometer or CAD visibility check against these angles. Pass if all are met.

extra.text: Unless specified otherwise, the values of the standard light distribution figures giving the minimum intensities for the various directions of measurement as a percentage of the minimum intensities required shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.
extra.test_case: Photometric goniometer measurement about the reference axis (H = 0°, V = 0°) through the centre of reference. Compute each grid-point minimum as the Figure A3-I percentage × the required minimum intensity, rounded down to three significant digits. Pass if every measured value ≥ its computed minimum.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer), the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check the declared mounting height of the rear position lamp. If it is ≤ 750 mm, verify Figure A3-I photometry only down to V = 5° downwards. Pass if all points within the reduced field meet their minima.

extra.text: If the stop lamp of category S1 or S2 is intended to be installed at a mounting height equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer), the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check the declared mounting height of the stop lamp. If it is ≤ 750 mm, verify Figure A3-I photometry only down to V = 5° downwards. Pass if all points within the reduced field meet their minima.

extra.text: The rear position lamp shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given in Figure A3-I as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Table 3).
extra.test_case: Goniometer measurement at all Figure A3-I measuring points. Pass if each point ≥ its percentage × the Table 3 minimum intensity.

extra.text: The stop lamp of category S1 or S2 shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given in Figure A3-I as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Table 7).
extra.test_case: Goniometer measurement at all Figure A3-I measuring points. Pass if each point ≥ its percentage × the Table 7 minimum intensity.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall emit, at the measuring points expressed in degrees of angle with the axis of reference, at least the minimum intensities in cd given in Figure A3-V.
extra.test_case: Goniometer measurement about the reference axis (H = 0°, V = 0°, horizontal and parallel to the vehicle median longitudinal plane) at each Figure A3-V point. Pass if each measured intensity ≥ the cd value shown.

extra.text: With respect to photometric performances, any rear combination lamp chosen at random from mass production shall meet the photometric requirements when tested according to paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Photometric test of a randomly selected production lamp per paragraph 4.8.; pass if conformity is not contestable under that paragraph.

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by mass-produced rear combination lamps shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement per paragraph 4.9.; pass if chromaticity coordinates lie within the prescribed colour boundaries for each function.

extra.text: With respect to photometric performance, when the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation are tested on any lamp chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per paragraph 4.8. on randomly chosen production lamps; pass if no measured value deviates from the values of paragraph 6.1.3.

extra.text: For the reversing lamp using light source technology other than incandescent only (LED), the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.1 after 1 min of operation; the distribution may be calculated from the distribution after photometric stability using the ratio of intensities at HV (1 min / stability). Pass: all test points within the min/max values of the reversing lamp requirements.

extra.text: For the rear position lamp using light source technology other than incandescent only (LED), the luminous intensities measured after 1 min of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.2 after 1 min of operation; may be calculated from the distribution after 30 min or after photometric stabilization using the HV intensity ratio. Pass: all test points within min/max.

extra.text: For the rear position lamp using light source technology other than incandescent only (LED), the luminous intensities measured either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.2 after 30 min of operation or after photometric stability. Pass: all test points within min/max.

extra.text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the rear position lamp shall additionally comply at 4 seconds after switch ON, with reference coordinate HV.
extra.test_case: Per Annex 8 para 2.1 / Table A8-1: check distribution at 4 s after switch ON (may be calculated from para 1 distribution using ratio at HV). Pass: min/max requirements met. For LED-only functions deemed compliant per para 2.1.2 if para 1.2 values comply.

extra.text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the stop lamp shall additionally comply at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, with reference coordinate HV.
extra.test_case: Per Annex 8 para 2.1 / Table A8-1: check distribution at 0.2 s after switch ON (may be calculated from para 1 distribution using ratio at HV). Pass: min/max requirements met. For LED-only functions deemed compliant per para 2.1.2 if para 1.2 values comply.

extra.text: The size of the approval marking shall comply with the value for 'a' defined in Table 1, with the arrangement of markings as shown in the examples in Annex 10.
extra.test_case: Measure the approval mark dimensions on the drawing and sample against the value 'a' in Table 1. Pass if dimensions are at or above the minimum.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter 'E' followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of drawing and sample. Pass if a circle surrounding 'E' with the country distinguishing number is present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection against the approval document. Pass if the correct 4–6 digit sequential number is marked.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the marking against the class symbol defined in paragraph 3.2.5 for the approved retro-reflector class (e.g. IA). Pass if the correct symbol is present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection. Pass if '150R' followed by the correct two-digit series of amendments (e.g. 150R00) is marked.

extra.text: In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflective device shall bear the word 'TOP' inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: Review the retro-reflector's rotational symmetry and the manufacturer's prescribed rotation angles. If orientation is ambiguous, inspect for a horizontal 'TOP' on the highest part of the illuminating surface. Pass if present when required.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the marking shall be visible after their installation.
extra.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the M1 vehicle (or a vehicle-representative fixture). Pass if the single marking is visible without removing the lamp.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
extra.test_case: Design review and disassembly check of every detachable light-transmitting part. Pass if each such part carries the mark, or its removal necessarily removes the mark.

extra.text: Retro-reflectors approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
extra.test_case: Production samples tested to the photometric, colorimetric and physical requirements of paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN R150; pass if samples conform to the approved type.

extra.text: The rear retro-reflector shall comply with the requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications", and in the Annexes referenced in those sections, of UN Regulation No. 48 and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval.
extra.test_case: Review of device design and installation data against UN R48 sections 5 and 6 and referenced Annexes (series in force at time of application); pass if all applicable rear retro-reflector provisions are met.

extra.text: The requirements of UN Regulation No. 48 pertinent to the rear retro-reflector and to vehicle category M1, on which the retro-reflecting device is intended to be installed, shall be applied where their verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: At device type approval, verify the R48 installation provisions for the rear retro-reflector on M1 that can be checked on the device (e.g. geometric visibility angles, orientation, illuminating surface, colour) using the device and intended mounting data; pass if all verifiable provisions are met.

extra.text: Any protuberances on the outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not prevent easy cleaning.
extra.test_case: Inspection of outer surface geometry; pass if protuberances do not hinder cleaning.

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall withstand the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6 (48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C) without distortion and, at least one hour after this test, shall meet the colorimetric requirements of paragraph 5.1.5. and the RI requirements of paragraph 5.1.4. for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: All ten samples: 48 h at 65 ± 2 °C per Part 1 Annex 6; visual check for distortion; after ≥1 h, colorimetry and RI at α = 20', β1 = β2 = 0° (or positions of Part 1 Annex 4 para 1.1/1.2); pass if no distortion and limits met; min and max samples then fully photometrically tested

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall pass the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and subsequently the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).
extra.test_case: First group (2 samples): water 10 min normal + 10 min inverted position, visual inspection; motor fuels 5 min and oils 5 min with visual inspection; then colour and RI at 20', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if no water penetration/damage and colour and RI comply

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall, if necessary, pass the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6 and then the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
extra.test_case: Second group (2 samples): corrosion 24 h, 2 h interval, 24 h, visual inspection; rear face abrasion 1 min, visual inspection; then colour and RI at 20', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if compliant

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall pass the test for stability in time of the optical properties of the retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Third group (2 samples): stability in time per Part 3 Annex 4; then colorimetry (visual or trichromatic) and RI at 20', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if compliant

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall pass the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
extra.test_case: Fourth group (2 samples): weathering per Part 6 Annex 6; then colorimetry and RI at 20', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if compliant

extra.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
extra.test_case: Colorimetry per paragraph 4.2 (visual, trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt) after each test group; pass if within red night-time limits

extra.text: Where more than one or a range of axes of reference are specified by the manufacturer, the retro-reflector shall meet the photometric requirements for each axis of reference or for the extreme axes of reference of the range specified.
extra.test_case: Repeat photometric measurements per Part 1 Annex 4 for each declared axis or extreme axes of range; pass if Table 3 values met each time

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 20' shall be equal to or greater than 3.00·10^2 mcd/lx at β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Photometry per para 3 Part 1 Annex 4, α = 20', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if RI ≥ 300 mcd/lx

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 1°30' shall be equal to or greater than 5 mcd/lx at β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Photometry, α = 1°30', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if RI ≥ 5 mcd/lx

extra.text: If the Class IA or IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values are verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: If declared mounting height < 750 mm, photometry for downward angles limited to 5°; pass if Table 3 values met within that range

extra.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux of the red retro-reflector must be within the limits for the night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
extra.test_case: Measure trichromatic coordinates of reflected light per para 4.2.1; pass if within UN R48 night-time red limits

extra.text: When testing the photometric performance of any mass-produced retro-reflective device chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of a randomly chosen production retro-reflector per this Regulation; retro-reflectors with apparent defects are disregarded; pass if no value is more than 20 per cent below the prescribed minimum.

extra.text: For testing the retro-reflection, the retro-reflective device shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Verify the source calibration certificate for CIE Illuminant A; pass if compliant.

extra.text: In the case of a moulded plastics reflector of a retro-reflecting device of Class IA or IB, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C for the resistance to heat test.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 1, para. 1: place the retro-reflector sample in a dry oven at 65 °C ± 2 °C for 48 consecutive hours. Pass: the exposure is completed and the sample proceeds to cooling and inspection.

extra.text: For the water penetration test, the retro-reflective device, whether part of a lamp or not, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.1: remove all removable parts; immerse 10 min in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with top of illuminating surface 20 mm below water surface; verify bath temperature, depth and duration are recorded.

extra.text: The 50 °C ± 5 °C immersion test of the retro-reflective device shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.1: invert device 180°, immerse 10 min at 50 °C ± 5 °C with rear face covered by about 20 mm of water.

extra.text: After the 50 °C immersions, the retro-reflective device sample units shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.1: immediately transfer to water at 25 °C ± 5 °C, same orientation/depth/duration conditions (thermal shock).

extra.text: If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water at the reflecting surface, the retro-reflective device shall not be considered to have passed the test.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection after immersion test; any clearly visible water = fail.

extra.text: If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage during the water spray test according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 3 2.2.3–2.2.4: energise the functions at design voltage, 5 min ON / 55 min OFF, for 12 cycles (12 hours). Spray conditions: solid cone nozzle at 45° ± 5° to vertical, precipitation 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min, device rotated at 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.

extra.text: After the water spray test and a drain period of 1 hour, no standing pool of water shall be formed in the interior of the device, nor be able to be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 3 2.2.5–2.2.6: after 12 h spray, stop rotation and spray, drain 1 h with cabinet door closed. Observe interior, then tap and tilt the device. Pass if no standing pool of water is present or formed.

extra.text: The device shall resist dust penetration that could significantly affect the photometric output of the retro-reflector when placed in the dust chamber no closer than 150 mm from a wall, with the test dust agitated at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 3 2.3.2–2.3.6: chamber cubical, 0.9 to 1.5 m per side, max 2 m3, charged with 3 to 5 kg fine powdered cement per ASTM C 150-84. Dust agitated by compressed air or blowers and allowed to settle between periods. Devices longer than 600 mm are horizontally centred.

extra.text: The lamp combined with the retro-reflective device shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
extra.test_case: Remove all removable parts; saline mist exposure 24 h + 2 h drying + 24 h; sample then assessed per paragraphs 4.1 and 4.2.

extra.text: After the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9.
extra.test_case: After 48 h recovery and cleaning of salt deposits, measure RA per Annex 6 Part 2 at β2 = 5°, α = 20'; pass if RA ≥ Table 9 value.

extra.text: The resistance to fuels test of the retro-reflective device shall be performed with a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 Part 1, para. 1: verify test fluid composition is 70 vol.% n-heptane / 30 vol.% toluol before applying to the retro-reflector; pass if the mixture is as specified.

extra.text: After about five minutes following the wiping with the test mixture, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall not show any apparent surface changes when inspected visually, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 Part 1, para. 1.1(b): about 5 minutes after wiping with the 70/30 n-heptane/toluol mixture, visually inspect the surface; pass if no apparent surface changes are found (slight surface cracks acceptable).

extra.text: It shall not be possible for the lamps of the rear combination lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.
extra.test_case: Design review and physical check of the mounting: attempt to fit and disturb the lamp in normal handling and service; pass if the lamp can only be mounted in the correct orientation and cannot change its aim/position without deliberate use of tools.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair (rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors) shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane, this estimate being based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.
extra.test_case: Measure the installed left and right lamps on the vehicle (e.g. CMM or vehicle drawing check) relative to the median longitudinal plane using the exterior geometrical form of each lamp; pass if the positions are mirror-symmetrical within measurement tolerance.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the left and right rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
extra.test_case: Compare left and right lamp exterior geometry (CAD and physical samples); pass if the exterior form is mirror-symmetrical about the median longitudinal plane; differences in interior structure (LED modules, PCB, reflector) are disregarded.
